statement: err_01 is the number of closed sites; err_02 lists the closed site IDs
Blue = active/open, grey = closed
err_01 == 256 is a read failure; drop the sample (252-255: A8; count-list gap: A15)
err_02 == N/A with err_01 == 0 means zero closed sites; keep
Trust list length over err_01 when they disagree
note: Data shows err_01 is never below list length -> list is a lower bound on closures; see A15 for the cut-off

statement: Each valid reading counts for the time until the next reading in the file, capped at 15 minutes: a dropped reading's own time is not counted; across a capture gap (missing rows) the last valid reading is carried forward for at most 15 minutes and gap time beyond that is not counted
note: DEFAULT_MAX_GAP_MIN=15 in lib/contactor_io.py. Corrected 2026-10-29: an earlier wording said the state carries across a dropped reading - it does not (verified on a synthetic example). Effect: weighted vs unweighted differs by ~0.65 pt on the front; caps of 15, 30 and unlimited give identical results, a cap of 5 shifts front by +0.4 pt. Analyst design choice - confirm with the owner

statement: Recency status uses the last 7 days of data: CURRENT/PERSISTENT/NEW = closed >= 50% of the window (NEW: < 20% before it), INTERMITTENT = 10-50%, RESOLVED = < 10% in the window but >= 10% over the period
note: Analyst design choice in chronic_sites.py (--recent-days 7); thresholds not yet confirmed with the process owner

statement: Time-series rules: anomaly flag at robust z > 2.5; a day is marked 'bad reads' at >= 5% failed readings; level shift = best single split (>= 7 days each side) with permutation p < 0.05; hour-of-day effect tested within day and re-tested without readings of >= 60 closed sites
note: Analyst design choices in daily_trend.py (a 3.5 threshold cannot fire on 32 days with ~2 pt daily noise); not confirmed with the process owner
